categories.name: Reader promise and original contribution
categories.evidence: The six-surface release envelope and evidence-impact set convert scattered settings into a reviewable engineering contract.

categories.name: Technical correctness and nuance
categories.evidence: The schema constrains array members, the resolver rejects unsafe paths, cross-field policy checks deny conflicting mutations, and provider-specific setting limits are qualified.

categories.name: Knowledge depth and progression
categories.evidence: One release-analyst case connects declared configuration, resolution, six surfaces, schema validation, evidence invalidation, and staged evaluation.

categories.name: Reproducibility and runnable evidence
categories.evidence: Pinned dependencies, configuration fixtures, a strict resolver, expected release record, and six tests reproduce accepted and rejected paths.

categories.name: Failures, trade-offs, and evaluation
categories.evidence: Unsafe overlays, malformed values, policy inconsistencies, alias ambiguity, cross-surface failures, and invalidated evidence are made explicit.

categories.name: Pedagogy and transfer
categories.evidence: The configuration exercise, change note, self-check, retrieval questions, and non-agent transfer prompt align with the outcomes.

categories.name: Visual explanation and accessibility
categories.evidence: Two captioned visuals show the six-surface envelope and the resolution/rejection pipeline with equivalent alt text and editable sources.

categories.name: Evidence and publishing trust
categories.evidence: Primary specifications, official guidance, practitioner synthesis, original tests, a claim register, disclosure, and limitations support the claims.
